sentences.text: This animal is distinguished by recurved spines along its sides that feature serrations on their front edges. In Sierritasuchus, the dorsal eminence extends to touch the posterior margin of the paramedian scute. Both the paramedian and lateral scutes of Sierritasuchus possess anterior bars.
Histological analysis of the scutes indicates the holotype individual was a subadult that had not reached full maturity.

Sierritasuchus is known from a small holotype skeleton found in the Late Triassic Tecovas Formation of Texas. The holotype skeleton, cataloged as UMMP V60817, was discovered in 1939 and was originally classified as Desmatosuchus.

The species was moved to its own genus in 2008, with the type species designated as S. macalpini. The genus name honors the location Sierrita de la Cruz Creek, while the species name honors the discoverer Archie MacAlpin.

Sierritasuchus is classified as an extinct genus of aetosaur belonging to the subfamily Desmatosuchinae. The parent group of Sierritasuchus is the tribe Desmatosuchini. Sierritasuchus belongs to the family Stagonolepididae.
Sierritasuchus lived during the Late Triassic period. The time range for Sierritasuchus spans from the Carnian to the Norian stages, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
